tagline: Over the Cumberland Plateau on a turnpike from 1801.
intro: From Carthage the byway crosses the Cumberland River and heads east on US 70N through Baxter and Cookeville, climbs onto the plateau at Monterey, and runs on through Crossville, Crab Orchard, Ozone and Rockwood to the Clinch River at Kingston. Most of the way it keeps close to the old Walton Road, and stretches of the original roadbed can still be seen from the highway.

Captain William Walton finished his road in 1801 as the Cumberland Turnpike, fifteen feet wide and free of stumps, with tollgates and a marker every three miles. A traveler in 1802 called it as broad and commodious as the roads around Philadelphia.

moments.title: Monterey
moments.text: The town grew around the Standing Stone, a guidepost for travelers, at the top of a 900-foot climb from White Plains that wore out people and animals alike.

moments.title: Ozone Falls
moments.text: A few hundred meters south of the highway Fall Creek drops 110 feet into a half-domed gorge, and migrants on the Walton Road wrote home about it.

moments.title: Fort Southwest Point
moments.text: On a hill above the meeting of the Clinch and the Tennessee, part of the 1797 frontier fort at the road's eastern end has been rebuilt on its original foundation.
